content: {"id": "51adf0b9-e597-4df2-b133-1cf0f8502b21", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "For an AWS Config resource type that changes many times per day, which recording mode is usually cheaper - continuous or daily - and why? No account access required.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "fc0ac716-7e31-4a59-83e8-394e38bb0bcf", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "AWS Config recording mode cost comparison analysis"}]}

{"id": "f22e6989-b047-4633-8066-d005c84fc203", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "For a resource type that changes many times per day, **daily recording mode is almost always cheaper**, and it's not close.

Here's why:

- **Continuous recording** creates a new configuration item (CI) every single time the resource's configuration changes — AWS Config bills per CI recorded. If a resource type changes dozens or hundreds of times a day, that's dozens or hundreds of billable CIs per resource, per day.
- **Daily recording mode** collapses this to at most **one CI per resource per day**, regardless of how many times it actually changed. AWS Config just captures the latest state once every 24 hours.

So the cost delta scales directly with change frequency: a resource changing 50 times/day costs roughly 50x more under continuous recording than under daily recording for that resource type. The trade-off is fidelity — with daily recording you lose the granular change history and point-in-time configuration snapshots between the daily captures, which matters if you rely on Config for detailed audit trails, compliance evidence of intermediate states, or fast drift detection tied to Config rules that evaluate on configuration change.

**Practical guidance:** use continuous recording selectively for resource types where every change genuinely needs to be captured (e.g., security groups, IAM policies) and switch high-churn, low-audit-value resource types (e.g., ECS task definitions, EC2 instance state changes, autoscaling-driven resources) to daily recording to cut costs.

If you want, I can pull up your actual Config recorder settings and identify which high-churn resource types in your account are currently on continuous recording and would benefit from switching.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
